- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. ## 1. Editor core

**Library:** TipTap 3 / ProseMirror. `package.json` pins `@tiptap/core` `^3.22.4`, `@tiptap/pm` `^3.22.4`, `@tiptap/starter-kit` `^3.22.4`, plus `extension-table`, `-table-row`, `-table-cell`, `-table-header`, `-text-style`, `-text-align`, `-link`, `-highlight`, `-image`, `-placeholder`, `-typography`, `-task-list/-item`, `-underline`, `-sub/superscript` (all 3.22.4). ## 2. Existing theme support: **none. Zero.**

```
grep -rniE "prefers-color-scheme|data-theme|darkMode|ThemeProvider|next-themes|useTheme|\.dark\b" \
```

Every one of those patterns returns nothing. There is:

- no `.dark` class, no `[data-theme]` selector
- no `prefers-color-scheme` media query anywhere
- no theme provider, no `next-themes`, no `useTheme`

The only media queries in `global.css` (9 total): **six** `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` (lines 1365, 1489, 1626, 2293, 2754, 3036), one `min-width: 768px` (2365), two `max-width: 640px` (2997, 3155). `src/components/ui/themed-dialog.tsx` is a misleading name — "themed" there means "styled to match the editorial aesthetic", not theme-switchable.

> - **Chrome uses `cssVar`**, so **a future theme can move it**.

## 3. Preferences / settings — two distinct patterns, pick the right one

### The settings page
`/home/diogenes/Projects/twyne/src/routes/settings/index.tsx` — **3266 lines**, one big `component$` with a flat `useStore<SettingsStore>` (lines 258–317). ### Pattern A — local-only preference (IndexedDB + localStorage), **not** synced to Convex

1. **Type + default** — `/home/diogenes/Projects/twyne/src/types/index.ts:789-811`

2. **Storage keys** — `/home/diogenes/Projects/twyne/src/utils/idb.ts:42-46`
   ```ts

   const WRITER_SETTINGS_STORAGE_KEY = "twyne.writer-settings.current";
   const APPARATUS_SETTINGS_STORAGE_KEY = "twyne.apparatus-settings.current";
   ```

3. **Read** — `loadApparatusSettingsFromIdb()`, `idb.ts:544-568`. Order is deliberate: bail to defaults if neither store exists → **localStorage first** (synchronous, fast) → IndexedDB `meta` object store fallback → defaults. Everything passes through a `normalizeApparatusSettings()` guard so corrupt JSON can't crash the app.

4. **Write** — `saveApparatusSettingsToIdb()`, `idb.ts:570-596`. Normalize → `writeLocalStorageJson(KEY, normalized)` → mirror into IDB `meta` as `{ key, value, updatedAt }`, all wrapped in `try/catch {}`.

5. **Load at mount** — `src/routes/settings/index.tsx:320-368`, a `useVisibleTask$` that `Promise.all`s the loaders and fans the result into `store`.

6. **Write on change** — `src/routes/settings/index.tsx:413-426`

   ```ts
     store.defaultCitationStyle = settings.defaultCitationStyle;
     /* … */
     await saveApparatusSettingsToIdb(settings);
     store.toast = "Preferences saved";
     setTimeout(() => (store.toast = null), 1800);
   ```

7. **Test precedent** — `/home/diogenes/Projects/twyne/src/utils/idb-preferences.test.ts` (~280 lines) shims `localStorage`, asserts localStorage is read *before* IndexedDB, and tests corrupt-blob recovery (`:254` writes `"{nope"`). Note the filename is `idb-preferences.test.ts` but the implementation lives in `idb.ts` — there is no `idb-preferences.ts`.

There is also a simpler single-value variant: `/home/diogenes/Projects/twyne/src/utils/auth-preference.ts` (key `twyne.auth.preferredMethod`, localStorage only, SSR-safe no-op outside browser) with `auth-preference.test.ts`. **For a theme preference this is arguably the better template** — a theme is one string, needs a synchronous read before paint, and IndexedDB is async so it can't participate in flash prevention.

### Pattern B — preference synced to Convex

Only **`roomSettings`** does this. Full chain:

1. **Schema** — `/home/diogenes/Projects/twyne/convex/schema.ts:163-168`
   ```ts
   // ── Room settings (tunable assistance) — one per user, latest wins. ──
   roomSettings: defineTable({
     userId: v.string(),
     settings: v.any(),
     updatedAt: v.number(),
   }).index("by_userId", ["userId"]),
   ```

2. **Query/mutation** — `/home/diogenes/Projects/twyne/convex/sync.ts:529-559`, `api.sync.getRoomSettings` and `api.sync.putRoomSettings`. Both `requireIdentity(ctx)` first; the mutation is an upsert on the `by_userId` index. Note `settings: v.any()` — schemaless blob, so adding a theme field needs **no migration**.

3. **Local mirror** — `/home/diogenes/Projects/twyne/src/utils/convex-sync.ts:848-866`, `saveRoomSettingsLocally()` / `loadRoomSettingsLocally()` (writes to `ROOM_SETTINGS_PATH` in the Lix file store, falls back to `DEFAULT_ROOM_SETTINGS`).

4. **The writer** — `/home/diogenes/Projects/twyne/src/components/personas/personas-panel.tsx:1460-1477`. This is the canonical local-first-then-sync shape:
   ```ts
   const persistSettings = $(async (next: RoomSettings) => {
     store.roomSettings = next;
     setBackgroundRoomEnabled(next.backgroundRoom !== false);   // apply immediately
     await saveRoomSettingsLocally(next);                        // local first
     const client =
       auth.value.provider === "convex" && auth.value.user ? clientSig.value : null;
     if (client) {
       try {
         await client.mutation(api.sync.putRoomSettings, { settings: next });
       } catch { /* sync will retry */ }
     }
   });
   ```
   Three things to copy verbatim for a theme: (a) mutate the store first so the UI is instant, (b) **apply the side effect immediately, not on next mount** — the comment at `:1462` says exactly why, (c) Convex write is best-effort behind an auth guard and a swallowed catch, because the app is offline-first.

5. **Readers** — `personas-panel.tsx:344` and `src/routes/editor/index.tsx:492-512` load it in a `Promise.all` at mount. Deleted with the account at `convex/account.ts:51`.

**Recommendation:** a theme preference is device-scoped, not account-scoped (people want dark on the laptop at night and light on the desktop), and it must be readable synchronously before first paint. So **Pattern A / `auth-preference.ts` style is the right base**, optionally with the Pattern B Convex tail if you want cross-device sync. Do **not** put it in `roomSettings` — that record is loaded async by the personas panel and editor, far too late to prevent a flash.

## Summary for a theming plan

**Green lights:**
- 1873 `var(--color-*)` call sites, 0 Tailwind color utilities, 13 stray hexes. A `[data-theme="dark"] { … }` override block redefining ~15 tokens gets you most of the way.
- 7 tokens (`--color-paper`, `-2`, `-3`, `-soft`, `--color-ink`, `-light`, `-muted`) + `--color-vermilion` cover ~90% of usage.
- `roomSettings` (`settings: v.any()`) accepts new fields with no Convex migration.
- Two clean, tested persistence patterns already exist.
- `palette.ts` already separates themeable `cssVar` from export-literal `hex`.
- `prefers-reduced-motion` is already honored — precedent for OS-preference respect.

2. **Flash-of-wrong-theme.** Qwik SSRs (`vite --mode ssr`), so `<html>` renders before any JS. Requires an inline `<script>` in `root.tsx`'s `<head>` reading localStorage and setting `data-theme` — no provider can do this.
3. **`<meta name="theme-color" content="#9c1a1f">`** hardcoded at `src/components/router-head/router-head.tsx:67`.

5. **3 undefined tokens** (`--color-accent` ×21, `--color-rule` ×2, `--color-crimson` ×1) and 10 undefined palette `cssVar`s — fix while in the token file.
6. **No Appearance section** in the 3266-line settings page; no Storybook theme decorator.
7. **~475 lines of dead variant CSS** (`.quarterly*`, gazette, halftone, paper-deckle) — delete rather than theme.

## 3. Preferences / settings — two distinct patterns, pick the right one

### The settings page
`/home/diogenes/Projects/twyne/src/routes/settings/index.tsx` — **3266 lines**, one big `component$` with a flat `useStore<SettingsStore>` (lines 258–317). Sections are `<section class="folio p-5">` with an `<h2>`; there are 9 of them (AI providers, per-feature overrides, apparatus/citations, writer profile, handle/profile, account, reset, delete). **There is no Appearance section** — that's where a theme control would slot in. It's the only route under `src/routes/settings/`.

### Pattern A — local-only preference (IndexedDB + localStorage), **not** synced to Convex

This is how `WriterSettings`, `ApparatusSettings`, and `AiSettings` work. Concrete end-to-end example — **`ApparatusSettings`**:

1. **Type + default** — `/home/diogenes/Projects/twyne/src/types/index.ts:789-811`
   ```ts
   export interface ApparatusSettings { defaultCitationStyle: ApparatusCitationStyle; aiEnhanceCitations: boolean; /* … */ }
   export const DEFAULT_APPARATUS_SETTINGS: ApparatusSettings = { defaultCitationStyle: "mla", /* … */ };
   ```
   (`WriterSettings` at `:769-780`.)

2. **Storage keys** — `/home/diogenes/Projects/twyne/src/utils/idb.ts:42-46`
   ```ts
   const AI_SETTINGS_STORAGE_KEY = "twyne.ai-settings.current";
   const WRITER_SETTINGS_STORAGE_KEY = "twyne.writer-settings.current";
   const APPARATUS_SETTINGS_STORAGE_KEY = "twyne.apparatus-settings.current";
   const WRITER_SETTINGS_META_KEY = "writer-settings";
   const APPARATUS_SETTINGS_META_KEY = "apparatus-settings";
   ```

3. **Read** — `loadApparatusSettingsFromIdb()`, `idb.ts:544-568`. Order is deliberate: bail to defaults if neither store exists → **localStorage first** (synchronous, fast) → IndexedDB `meta` object store fallback → defaults. Everything passes through a `normalizeApparatusSettings()` guard so corrupt JSON can't crash the app.

4. **Write** — `saveApparatusSettingsToIdb()`, `idb.ts:570-596`. Normalize → `writeLocalStorageJson(KEY, normalized)` → mirror into IDB `meta` as `{ key, value, updatedAt }`, all wrapped in `try/catch {}`.

5. **Load at mount** — `src/routes/settings/index.tsx:320-368`, a `useVisibleTask$` that `Promise.all`s the loaders and fans the result into `store`.

6. **Write on change** — `src/routes/settings/index.tsx:413-426`
   ```ts
   const persistApparatusSettings = $(async (settings: ApparatusSettings) => {
     store.defaultCitationStyle = settings.defaultCitationStyle;
     /* … */
     await saveApparatusSettingsToIdb(settings);
     store.toast = "Preferences saved";
     setTimeout(() => (store.toast = null), 1800);
   });
   ```
   (`setWriterStyle` at `:388-401` and `saveWriterProfile` at `:403-411` are the same shape.)

7. **Test precedent** — `/home/diogenes/Projects/twyne/src/utils/idb-preferences.test.ts` (~280 lines) shims `localStorage`, asserts localStorage is read *before* IndexedDB, and tests corrupt-blob recovery (`:254` writes `"{nope"`). Note the filename is `idb-preferences.test.ts` but the implementation lives in `idb.ts` — there is no `idb-preferences.ts`.

There is also a simpler single-value variant: `/home/diogenes/Projects/twyne/src/utils/auth-preference.ts` (key `twyne.auth.preferredMethod`, localStorage only, SSR-safe no-op outside browser) with `auth-preference.test.ts`. **For a theme preference this is arguably the better template** — a theme is one string, needs a synchronous read before paint, and IndexedDB is async so it can't participate in flash prevention.

### Pattern B — preference synced to Convex

Only **`roomSettings`** does this. Full chain:

1. **Schema** — `/home/diogenes/Projects/twyne/convex/schema.ts:163-168`
   ```ts
   // ── Room settings (tunable assistance) — one per user, latest wins. ──
   roomSettings: defineTable({
     userId: v.string(),
     settings: v.any(),
     updatedAt: v.number(),
   }).index("by_userId", ["userId"]),
   ```

2. **Query/mutation** — `/home/diogenes/Projects/twyne/convex/sync.ts:529-559`, `api.sync.getRoomSettings` and `api.sync.putRoomSettings`. Both `requireIdentity(ctx)` first; the mutation is an upsert on the `by_userId` index. Note `settings: v.any()` — schemaless blob, so adding a theme field needs **no migration**.

3. **Local mirror** — `/home/diogenes/Projects/twyne/src/utils/convex-sync.ts:848-866`, `saveRoomSettingsLocally()` / `loadRoomSettingsLocally()` (writes to `ROOM_SETTINGS_PATH` in the Lix file store, falls back to `DEFAULT_ROOM_SETTINGS`).

4. **The writer** — `/home/diogenes/Projects/twyne/src/components/personas/personas-panel.tsx:1460-1477`. This is the canonical local-first-then-sync shape:
   ```ts
   const persistSettings = $(async (next: RoomSettings) => {
     store.roomSettings = next;
     setBackgroundRoomEnabled(next.backgroundRoom !== false);   // apply immediately
     await saveRoomSettingsLocally(next);                        // local first
     const client =
       auth.value.provider === "convex" && auth.value.user ? clientSig.value : null;
     if (client) {
       try {
         await client.mutation(api.sync.putRoomSettings, { settings: next });
       } catch { /* sync will retry */ }
     }
   });
   ```
   Three things to copy verbatim for a theme: (a) mutate the store first so the UI is instant, (b) **apply the side effect immediately, not on next mount** — the comment at `:1462` says exactly why, (c) Convex write is best-effort behind an auth guard and a swallowed catch, because the app is offline-first.

5. **Readers** — `personas-panel.tsx:344` and `src/routes/editor/index.tsx:492-512` load it in a `Promise.all` at mount. Deleted with the account at `convex/account.ts:51`.

**Recommendation:** a theme preference is device-scoped, not account-scoped (people want dark on the laptop at night and light on the desktop), and it must be readable synchronously before first paint. So **Pattern A / `auth-preference.ts` style is the right base**, optionally with the Pattern B Convex tail if you want cross-device sync. Do **not** put it in `roomSettings` — that record is loaded async by the personas panel and editor, far too late to prevent a flash.

## Summary for a theming plan

**Green lights:**
- 1873 `var(--color-*)` call sites, 0 Tailwind color utilities, 13 stray hexes. A `[data-theme="dark"] { … }` override block redefining ~15 tokens gets you most of the way.
- 7 tokens (`--color-paper`, `-2`, `-3`, `-soft`, `--color-ink`, `-light`, `-muted`) + `--color-vermilion` cover ~90% of usage.
- `roomSettings` (`settings: v.any()`) accepts new fields with no Convex migration.
- Two clean, tested persistence patterns already exist.
- `palette.ts` already separates themeable `cssVar` from export-literal `hex`.
- `prefers-reduced-motion` is already honored — precedent for OS-preference respect.

**Obstacles, in priority order:**
1. **103 hardcoded `rgba()` values in `global.css`** — the real work. Paper grain (`:85-100`), `.folio` shadows (`:423-431`), `.ink-bleed` (`:1763`), `.paper-sheet` foxing (`:1643`), `.paper-foxed`, `.halftone` all bake `rgba(31,27,22,…)` ink and `rgba(255,255,255,0.6)` highlights. On a dark ground these invert wrongly. Needs a `--grain-color` / `--emboss-highlight` / `--ink-bleed-shadow` layer.
2. **Flash-of-wrong-theme.** Qwik SSRs (`vite --mode ssr`), so `<html>` renders before any JS. Requires an inline `<script>` in `root.tsx`'s `<head>` reading localStorage and setting `data-theme` — no provider can do this.
3. **`<meta name="theme-color" content="#9c1a1f">`** hardcoded at `src/components/router-head/router-head.tsx:67`.
4. **13 TSX hexes + heatmap ramp** (`writing-heatmap.tsx:26-28`) need tokenizing.
5. **3 undefined tokens** (`--color-accent` ×21, `--color-rule` ×2, `--color-crimson` ×1) and 10 undefined palette `cssVar`s — fix while in the token file.
6. **No Appearance section** in the 3266-line settings page; no Storybook theme decorator.
7. **~475 lines of dead variant CSS** (`.quarterly*`, gazette, halftone, paper-deckle) — delete rather than theme.

content.text: I have a clear picture. Three decisions shape the plan — let me confirm them with you.

questions.question: Spellcheck: the browser gives you red squiggles but exposes NO API to read them or open the native suggestion menu. The only keyboard path to native suggestions is the OS context-menu key (Shift+F10 / ≣), which already works today. So "hands-off spelling via hotkeys" requires our own dictionary. How far do you want to go?

options.label: In-app dictionary + hotkeys
options.description: Lazy-load nspell + dictionary-en (~1MB, fetched on first use, opt-in in settings). ProseMirror decoration plugin underlines misspellings. New registry commands: F7 = next misspelling, Mod-. = suggestions popup at caret (Enter/arrows to accept), Add to dictionary. Personal dictionary persisted locally. Real work: ~2-3 days, new dep + async load path.
options.preview:
EDITOR_KEYBINDINGS additions:
  spelling.next        F7
  spelling.previous    Shift-F7
  spelling.suggest     Mod-.
  spelling.toggle      (settings only)

Caret in "recieve" → Mod-. →
  ┌──────────────┐
  │ receive      │ ← Enter
  │ relieve      │
  │ ──────────── │
  │ Add to dict  │
  └──────────────┘

options.label: Native only — document it
options.description: No engine. Set spellcheck=true explicitly on the ProseMirror surface, add a per-document spellcheck toggle, and document Shift+F10 / ≣ in the shortcuts dialog + Manual as the way to reach browser suggestions. ~2 hours. Honest but thin — you can't jump to the *next* misspelling, only act on the word under the caret.
options.preview:
Shortcuts dialog gains:

  SPELLING
  Suggestions for word    Shift+F10
  under caret             (or ≣ Menu key)

  Uses your browser's built-in
  dictionary. Twyne does not
  check spelling itself.

options.label: Defer spellcheck
options.description: Skip it this round; ship the marginalia fix, tables, and theming. Revisit once you see whether more than one user asks.

questions.question: Theming: the codebase is unusually ready — 1873 `var(--color-*)` call sites, zero Tailwind color utilities, and ~7 tokens carry 90% of the UI. There is currently no theme layer at all. How much do you want to build?

options.label: Presets + custom core colors
options.description: A [data-theme] layer with 4 presets (Editorial = today's cream, Foolscap = cool grey-white low-chroma, Broadsheet = high-contrast near-white, Nightpress = dark) PLUS an Appearance section in settings letting you override the ~8 core tokens with the existing color-picker, live preview, and a WCAG contrast warning.     ),

      transparent 1.4px
    );

    auto,

# Marginalia mentions, table deletion, and a theme layer

## Context

Feedback from a user (tryingET) surfaced three problems, two of them bugs:

1. **Marginalia @-mentions drop the name.** Typing `@`, then picking a suggestion **with the mouse**, leaves only the bare `@` — the inserted name never lands. Keyboard selection isn't an alternative because it was never implemented.
2. **Tables can't be fully deleted.** The first row can't be deleted (the second row's button works), and there's no apparent way to remove the table itself.
3. **The palette is hard on the eyes.** The reporter is a light-mode user who doesn't want dark mode — they want *different colors*. There is no theme layer in the app at all today.

Spellcheck was also raised and has been **explicitly dropped from scope** — the browser exposes no API to read squiggles or open the native suggestion menu, so "hands-off spelling by hotkey" would mean shipping our own dictionary engine, which isn't worth it right now.

Two facts shape the whole plan:

- **This is Qwik, not React.** `component$`, `useStore`, `useVisibleTask$`, QRLs. Event handlers ending in `$` are *asynchronously loaded* — that is the direct cause of bug #1, and it's why the theme flash-guard must be an inline `<script>` rather than a provider.
- **The codebase is unusually ready for theming.** 1873 `var(--color-*)` call sites, **zero** Tailwind color utilities, zero arbitrary hex classes, and just 7 tokens carry ~90% of the UI.

---

## 1. Marginalia @-mentions

The `@`-picker is not a TipTap suggestion plugin — it's plain textarea logic in the comments panel. Four separate defects stack up.

**Files:** `src/components/ui/mention-dropdown.tsx`, `src/utils/mentions.ts`, `src/components/comments/comments-panel.tsx` (two call sites: new-note `:508-552`, reply `:842-893`).

### a. The mouse-pick race — the actual reported bug

`mention-dropdown.tsx:33` guards blur with `onMouseDown$={(e) => e.preventDefault()}`. In Qwik that handler is a QRL: on first interaction its chunk is fetched **asynchronously**, so `preventDefault()` runs after the browser has already dispatched the default mousedown. Sequence: mousedown → textarea blurs → `onBlur$` sets `mentionTarget = null` (`comments-panel.tsx:531-533`, `:871-874`) → dropdown unmounts before mouseup → **no `click` event ever fires** → `onSelect$` never runs → text stays `"@"`.

Fix: use Qwik's declarative `preventdefault:mousedown` JSX attribute, which is applied at serialization time and needs no JS. Already the house idiom — `twyne-editor.tsx:3812-3814`, `auth-panel.tsx:504`, `routes/downloads/index.tsx:129`. Put it on the dropdown **container**, not just each button, so clicks on padding don't blur either.

### b. Blur handler is unconditional

Belt-and-braces so this can't regress: in both `onBlur$` handlers, only clear `mentionTarget` when the blur is leaving the mention UI — check `relatedTarget` against a `data-mention-dropdown` container attribute added in `mention-dropdown.tsx`.

### c. No keyboard path exists at all

The textarea `onKeyDown$` handlers (`:522-530`, `:856-870`) only handle `Escape` and `Mod+Enter`. Add an `activeIndex` to the store, handle `ArrowUp`/`ArrowDown`/`Enter`/`Tab` (with `preventDefault` so Enter doesn't insert a newline), reset the index on every `onInput$`, and pass `activeIndex` into `MentionDropdown` for highlight styling + `aria-activedescendant`. Mirror the working pattern in `src/components/editor/slash-command-menu.tsx:49-71`.

### d. Mentions only work at end-of-text

`activeMentionQuery` (`mentions.ts:19-22`) matches `/@([A-Za-z]*)$/` against the whole value, and `applyMention` (`:25-27`) replaces the *last* match. So mid-text mentions never trigger, and editing earlier in a note rewrites the wrong `@`.

Change both to be caret-aware: `activeMentionQuery(value, caret)` matches against `value.slice(0, caret)`; `applyMention(value, name, caret)` returns `{ text, caret }` so the callers can restore the cursor after the inserted name. Widen the character class beyond `[A-Za-z]` to cover digits/hyphens.

> **Check during implementation:** whether persona names contain spaces. If they do, `filterMentionables`' `startsWith` and `mentionedIn`'s `@Name\b` regex are both already broken for those names — flag it, don't silently expand scope.

**Tests:** extend the existing `src/utils/mentions.test.ts` with caret-aware cases (mention mid-sentence, two `@`s in one note, caret position after insert). Add an active-item story to `src/components/ui/mention-dropdown.stories.tsx`.

---

## 2. Tables

### a. First row not deletable — finish the in-progress fix

This is **not** an availability bug. `getTableActionAvailability` (`extensions/table-format.ts:525-544`) mirrors `editor.can().deleteRow()`, which ProseMirror implements as `isInTable(state)` — essentially always true. The button is enabled and the command works.

The real cause is that **the cell-format panel physically covers row 1**. The committed code renders it at `store.tableToolbar.position.top + 120` (`twyne-editor.tsx:3656-3659`). The toolbar is normally placed `"above"` with `desiredTop = anchor.top - height - gap` where height=112, gap=8 — so `position.top ≈ anchor.top - 120`, putting the panel's top at exactly `anchor.top`, on the first row, at `z-index: var(--z-dropdown)`, eating every click. Row 2 sits below the panel, which is precisely the reported asymmetry. The panel shows almost always, since `getSelectedCellFormat` returns 1 cell for a plain caret.

The **uncommitted working-tree diff already fixes this** — it adds `computeTableToolbarStackPosition()` which measures placement against the combined toolbar+panel height and returns an explicit `cellRowTop`. Finish it, plus one hardening change:

- `TABLE_TOOLBAR_IDEAL_HEIGHT` (112) and the new `TABLE_CELL_FORMAT_PANEL_HEIGHT` (68) are **hardcoded guesses, never measured**. A font, zoom, or button-wrap difference re-creates the exact overlap. Keep them as the first-paint estimate, then after render measure the real element (`[data-floating-table-toolbar]`) with `getBoundingClientRect()` and recompute. Otherwise this bug comes back on someone else's machine.
- Extend `floating-table-toolbar.test.ts` (which already gained 3 tests) with a measured-height case asserting `cellRowTop + panelHeight <= anchor.top` when placed above.

### b. "Can't get rid of the table" — reachability, not a missing feature

`deleteTable` exists and works (`table-format.ts:502-507`, dispatched at `:614-615`). It's simply **unreachable**:

- It's the last of 12 text-labelled buttons in a `flex min-w-max` row (`floating-table-toolbar.tsx:315`) inside a container capped at `TABLE_TOOLBAR_IDEAL_WIDTH = 760` with `overflow-x-auto`. At ~90-110px per label the row is 1100px+, so "Delete table" sits off the right edge behind a horizontal scroll nobody discovers.
- There is **no** `table.delete-row` / `table.delete-column` / `table.delete-table` in `EDITOR_COMMANDS` at all — so no slash menu, no shortcut dialog, no Manual entry. Only add/merge/split are registered (`editor-commands.ts:475-523`).

Two changes:

1. **Register the missing commands.** Add the three definitions to `src/utils/editor-commands.ts` with `availability: "table"`, alongside the existing table entries. Wiring is nearly free — `TABLE_COMMAND_MAP` in `twyne-editor.tsx:92-97` just needs three more lines (`"table.delete-row": "deleteRow"`, etc.); the executor cases already exist at `:2393`, `:2402`, `:2417`. Include them in the `slash` surface so `/delete table` works, and give `table.delete-table` a keybinding in `EDITOR_KEYBINDINGS`.
2. **Pin the destructive cluster in the toolbar.** Pull `deleteRow` / `deleteColumn` / `deleteTable` out of the scrolling row into a trailing group with `sticky right-0` and a paper background, so they stay visible regardless of horizontal scroll position. Keeps the text labels (destructive actions shouldn't be icon-only) while making them reachable.

---

## 3. Theming

### Why this is cheap here

| | |
|---|---|
| `var(--color-*)` call sites in TSX | **1873** |
| Tailwind color utilities / arbitrary hex in TSX | **0** |
| Raw hex literals in TSX | 13 (7 files) |
| Tokens covering ~90% of usage | **7** (`--color-paper`, `-2`, `-3`, `-soft`, `--color-ink`, `-light`, `-muted`) + `--color-vermilion` |

Tokens live in a Tailwind v4 `@theme` block at `src/global.css:13-63`. There is no `tailwind.config.*` — the entire Tailwind setup is the Vite plugin. There is **no** existing theme support: `prefers-color-scheme`, `data-theme`, `.dark`, `darkMode`, `ThemeProvider`, `useTheme` all return zero matches repo-wide.

### The one real obstacle: baked-in rgba

103 `rgba()` literals in `global.css` hardcode the palette into textures — paper grain (`:85-100`), `.folio` shadows (`:423-431`), `.ink-bleed` (`:1763`), `.paper-sheet` foxing (`:1643`). On a different ground these invert wrongly (a white inset highlight on dark paper reads as a scratch).

But they're highly concentrated, and the fix is mechanical:

| literal | count | becomes |
|---|---|---|
| `rgba(31, 27, 22, α)` | **52** | `color-mix(in srgb, var(--color-ink) α%, transparent)` |
| `rgba(255, 255, 255, α)` | 10 | `var(--emboss-highlight)` (new token) |
| `rgba(193, 39, 45, α)` | 9 | `color-mix(… var(--color-vermilion) …)` |
| `rgba(92, 107, 192, α)` | 6 | `color-mix(… var(--color-periwinkle) …)` |

1. **`src/utils/theme.ts`** (new). `ThemePreference = { preset: ThemePresetId; custom?: Partial<Record<ThemeTokenId, string>> }`; `THEME_PRESETS`; `readThemePreference()` / `writeThemePreference()`; `applyTheme(pref, root)` stamping `data-theme` plus `style.setProperty` for custom overrides; `contrastRatio(a, b)` for the WCAG guard. Follow `src/utils/auth-preference.ts` exactly for storage shape — SSR-safe `getStorage()`, swallowed writes, corrupt-blob wipe. Key: `twyne.appearance.theme`.
2. **`src/global.css`** — add `[data-theme="…"]` blocks redefining the core tokens per preset. Presets: **Editorial** (today's cream, default), **Foolscap** (cool low-chroma grey-white — the direct answer to this user's complaint), **Broadsheet** (high-contrast near-white), **Nightpress** (dark). Also add a `System` mode honoring `prefers-color-scheme`; precedent exists, `prefers-reduced-motion` is already respected in 6 places.
3. **Tokenize the textures** per the table above; add `--emboss-highlight`, `--grain-ink`, `--ink-bleed-shadow`, `--folio-shadow`.
4. **Define the 3 missing tokens.** `--color-accent` (21 uses), `--color-rule` (2), `--color-crimson` (1) are referenced but **defined nowhere** — currently rendering as `unset`. Same for 10 phantom `cssVar`s named in `src/utils/palette.ts`. Fix while in the file.
5. **Flash guard** — inline `<script>` in `root.tsx`'s `<head>` (before `<RouterHead/>`, `root.tsx:23-43`) reading localStorage and stamping `document.documentElement` before first paint. **Must be inline**: Qwik SSRs, so `<html>` renders before any QRL resumes — no provider can do this.
6. **`router-head.tsx:67`** — `<meta name="theme-color" content="#9c1a1f">` is hardcoded; make it theme-reactive.
7. **Settings → Appearance.** New `<section class="folio p-5">` in `src/routes/settings/index.tsx` (9 sections today, none for appearance). Preset picker + collapsible custom palette over the 8 core tokens, reusing `src/components/ui/color-picker.tsx`. Apply to `document.documentElement` **immediately on change**, not on next mount — the precedent and its rationale are at `personas-panel.tsx:1460-1477`. Show the WCAG ink-on-paper ratio with a warning under 4.5:1.
8. **Persist local-first, sync best-effort.** localStorage write (synchronous, feeds the flash guard) → then `api.sync.putRoomSettings` behind the auth guard in a swallowed `try/catch`, copying the shape of `persistSettings` (`personas-panel.tsx:1460-1477`). Add an `appearance` key to the `roomSettings` blob — `convex/schema.ts:163-168` types it `v.any()`, so **no migration**. On load, local wins for first paint; reconcile from remote afterwards only when remote `updatedAt` is newer.
9. **Storybook** — add a theme decorator to `.storybook/preview.ts` (currently just imports `global.css`).
10. **Cleanup while in these files** — tokenize the 13 TSX hexes (`writing-heatmap.tsx:26-28` ramp, `anti-tabula-rasa.tsx:388`, `twyne-editor.tsx:2678,2684`, `color-picker.tsx:77`), and **delete** ~475 lines of dead landing-variant CSS (`global.css:1816-2291` — `.quarterly*`, gazette, `.halftone`, `.paper-deckle` all have zero TSX usages). Don't theme dead code.

### Constraint: don't theme document content

`src/utils/palette.ts:29-31` deliberately splits literal `hex` (written into documents, must survive export) from `cssVar` (app chrome, themeable). **Theming touches only the `cssVar` side.** Text colors and highlights the writer applied are baked into exported documents and must not shift when the app theme changes. The author already anticipated this — honor the split.

---

## Verification

**Unit tests** (per `bun test <file>`, individually — full-suite runs flake from known cross-file interference):

```

bun test src/utils/mentions.test.ts
bun test src/utils/theme.test.ts          # new
bun test src/utils/palette.test.ts        # guard the hex/cssVar split
```

**Manual, in the dev server:**

- *Mentions*: in the marginalia panel, type `@` + a partial name, click a suggestion **with the mouse** → full name inserted. Repeat with arrows + Enter. Type a mention mid-sentence, not at the end. Do it in both the new-note and the reply textarea.

- Run `tsc` — the token IDs and `EditorCommandId` union are typed, so most wiring mistakes surface there.

## Out of scope

- **Spellcheck** — dropped per your call. Worth recording *why*, so it doesn't get relitigated: browsers give no API to read squiggle positions or open the native suggestion menu, so this would mean bundling a dictionary engine.
- Space-containing persona names in mentions (pre-existing, flag if hit).
- Widening the theme editor beyond the 8 core tokens.

# Marginalia mentions, table deletion, and a theme layer

## Context

Feedback from a user (tryingET) surfaced three problems, two of them bugs:

1. **Marginalia @-mentions drop the name.** Typing `@`, then picking a suggestion **with the mouse**, leaves only the bare `@` — the inserted name never lands. Keyboard selection isn't an alternative because it was never implemented.
2. **Tables can't be fully deleted.** The first row can't be deleted (the second row's button works), and there's no apparent way to remove the table itself.
3. **The palette is hard on the eyes.** The reporter is a light-mode user who doesn't want dark mode — they want *different colors*. There is no theme layer in the app at all today.

Spellcheck was also raised and has been **explicitly dropped from scope** — the browser exposes no API to read squiggles or open the native suggestion menu, so "hands-off spelling by hotkey" would mean shipping our own dictionary engine, which isn't worth it right now.

Two facts shape the whole plan:

- **This is Qwik, not React.** `component$`, `useStore`, `useVisibleTask$`, QRLs. Event handlers ending in `$` are *asynchronously loaded* — that is the direct cause of bug #1, and it's why the theme flash-guard must be an inline `<script>` rather than a provider.
- **The codebase is unusually ready for theming.** 1873 `var(--color-*)` call sites, **zero** Tailwind color utilities, zero arbitrary hex classes, and just 7 tokens carry ~90% of the UI.

---

## 1. Marginalia @-mentions

**Files:** `src/components/ui/mention-dropdown.tsx`, `src/utils/mentions.ts`, `src/components/comments/comments-panel.tsx` (two call sites: new-note `:508-552`, reply `:842-893`).

### a. The mouse-pick race — the actual reported bug

`mention-dropdown.tsx:33` guards blur with `onMouseDown$={(e) => e.preventDefault()}`. In Qwik that handler is a QRL: on first interaction its chunk is fetched **asynchronously**, so `preventDefault()` runs after the browser has already dispatched the default mousedown. Sequence: mousedown → textarea blurs → `onBlur$` sets `mentionTarget = null` (`comments-panel.tsx:531-533`, `:871-874`) → dropdown unmounts before mouseup → **no `click` event ever fires** → `onSelect$` never runs → text stays `"@"`.

Fix: use Qwik's declarative `preventdefault:mousedown` JSX attribute, which is applied at serialization time and needs no JS. Already the house idiom — `twyne-editor.tsx:3812-3814`, `auth-panel.tsx:504`, `routes/downloads/index.tsx:129`. Put it on the dropdown **container**, not just each button, so clicks on padding don't blur either.

### b. Blur handler is unconditional

Belt-and-braces so this can't regress: in both `onBlur$` handlers, only clear `mentionTarget` when the blur is leaving the mention UI — check `relatedTarget` against a `data-mention-dropdown` container attribute added in `mention-dropdown.tsx`.

### c. No keyboard path exists at all

The textarea `onKeyDown$` handlers (`:522-530`, `:856-870`) only handle `Escape` and `Mod+Enter`. Add an `activeIndex` to the store, handle `ArrowUp`/`ArrowDown`/`Enter`/`Tab` (with `preventDefault` so Enter doesn't insert a newline), reset the index on every `onInput$`, and pass `activeIndex` into `MentionDropdown` for highlight styling + `aria-activedescendant`. Mirror the working pattern in `src/components/editor/slash-command-menu.tsx:49-71`.

### d. Mentions only work at end-of-text

`activeMentionQuery` (`mentions.ts:19-22`) matches `/@([A-Za-z]*)$/` against the whole value, and `applyMention` (`:25-27`) replaces the *last* match. So mid-text mentions never trigger, and editing earlier in a note rewrites the wrong `@`.

Change both to be caret-aware: `activeMentionQuery(value, caret)` matches against `value.slice(0, caret)`; `applyMention(value, name, caret)` returns `{ text, caret }` so the callers can restore the cursor after the inserted name. > **Check during implementation:** whether persona names contain spaces. If they do, `filterMentionables`' `startsWith` and `mentionedIn`'s `@Name\b` regex are both already broken for those names — flag it, don't silently expand scope.

---

### a. First row not deletable — finish the in-progress fix

This is **not** an availability bug. `getTableActionAvailability` (`extensions/table-format.ts:525-544`) mirrors `editor.can().deleteRow()`, which ProseMirror implements as `isInTable(state)` — essentially always true. The button is enabled and the command works.

### Why this is cheap here

| | |

## Context

Feedback from a user (tryingET) surfaced three problems, two of them bugs:

1. **Marginalia @-mentions drop the name.** Typing `@`, then picking a suggestion **with the mouse**, leaves only the bare `@` — the inserted name never lands. Keyboard selection isn't an alternative because it was never implemented.
2. **Tables can't be fully deleted.** The first row can't be deleted (the second row's button works), and there's no apparent way to remove the table itself.
3. **The palette is hard on the eyes.** The reporter is a light-mode user who doesn't want dark mode — they want *different colors*. There is no theme layer in the app at all today.

Spellcheck was also raised and has been **explicitly dropped from scope** — the browser exposes no API to read squiggles or open the native suggestion menu, so "hands-off spelling by hotkey" would mean shipping our own dictionary engine, which isn't worth it right now.

Two facts shape the whole plan:

- **This is Qwik, not React.** `component$`, `useStore`, `useVisibleTask$`, QRLs. Event handlers ending in `$` are *asynchronously loaded* — that is the direct cause of bug #1, and it's why the theme flash-guard must be an inline `<script>` rather than a provider.
- **The codebase is unusually ready for theming.** 1873 `var(--color-*)` call sites, **zero** Tailwind color utilities, zero arbitrary hex classes, and just 7 tokens carry ~90% of the UI.

---

## 1. Marginalia @-mentions

The `@`-picker is not a TipTap suggestion plugin — it's plain textarea logic in the comments panel. Four separate defects stack up.

**Files:** `src/components/ui/mention-dropdown.tsx`, `src/utils/mentions.ts`, `src/components/comments/comments-panel.tsx` (two call sites: new-note `:508-552`, reply `:842-893`).

### a. The mouse-pick race — the actual reported bug

`mention-dropdown.tsx:33` guards blur with `onMouseDown$={(e) => e.preventDefault()}`. In Qwik that handler is a QRL: on first interaction its chunk is fetched **asynchronously**, so `preventDefault()` runs after the browser has already dispatched the default mousedown. Sequence: mousedown → textarea blurs → `onBlur$` sets `mentionTarget = null` (`comments-panel.tsx:531-533`, `:871-874`) → dropdown unmounts before mouseup → **no `click` event ever fires** → `onSelect$` never runs → text stays `"@"`.

Fix: use Qwik's declarative `preventdefault:mousedown` JSX attribute, which is applied at serialization time and needs no JS. Already the house idiom — `twyne-editor.tsx:3812-3814`, `auth-panel.tsx:504`, `routes/downloads/index.tsx:129`. Put it on the dropdown **container**, not just each button, so clicks on padding don't blur either.

### b. Blur handler is unconditional

Belt-and-braces so this can't regress: in both `onBlur$` handlers, only clear `mentionTarget` when the blur is leaving the mention UI — check `relatedTarget` against a `data-mention-dropdown` container attribute added in `mention-dropdown.tsx`.

### c. No keyboard path exists at all

The textarea `onKeyDown$` handlers (`:522-530`, `:856-870`) only handle `Escape` and `Mod+Enter`. Add an `activeIndex` to the store, handle `ArrowUp`/`ArrowDown`/`Enter`/`Tab` (with `preventDefault` so Enter doesn't insert a newline), reset the index on every `onInput$`, and pass `activeIndex` into `MentionDropdown` for highlight styling + `aria-activedescendant`. Mirror the working pattern in `src/components/editor/slash-command-menu.tsx:49-71`.

### d. Mentions only work at end-of-text

`activeMentionQuery` (`mentions.ts:19-22`) matches `/@([A-Za-z]*)$/` against the whole value, and `applyMention` (`:25-27`) replaces the *last* match. So mid-text mentions never trigger, and editing earlier in a note rewrites the wrong `@`.

content.subject: Fix marginalia @-mention selection
content.description: Fix the Qwik QRL mousedown race that drops the mention, guard the blur handler, add keyboard nav (arrows/Enter/Tab), and make activeMentionQuery/applyMention caret-aware. Files: mention-dropdown.tsx, mentions.ts, comments-panel.tsx (2 call sites). Extend mentions.test.ts.

content.subject: Finish table toolbar stack positioning
content.description: Complete the in-progress computeTableToolbarStackPosition work so the cell-format panel never covers the table's first row. Replace hardcoded 112/68 height guesses with measured getBoundingClientRect after render. Extend floating-table-toolbar.test.ts.

content.subject: Make table delete actions reachable
content.description: Register table.delete-row / delete-column / delete-table in EDITOR_COMMANDS, wire TABLE_COMMAND_MAP in twyne-editor.tsx, expose in slash menu + a keybinding, and pin the destructive cluster sticky right-0 in the floating toolbar so it survives horizontal scroll.

content.subject: Build theme token foundation

input.new_string:
<textarea
              id={mentionInputId("new")}
              value={store.newCommentText}
              aria-label="New margin note"
              role="combobox"
              aria-expanded={store.mentionTarget === "new"}
              aria-controls={mentionListId("new")}
              aria-activedescendant={
                store.mentionTarget === "new"
                  ? mentionOptionId(
                      mentionListId("new"),
                      filterMentionables(mentionables, store.mentionQuery)[
                        store.mentionIndex
                      ]?.id ?? "",
                    )
                  : undefined
              }
              onInput$={(e) => {
                const el = e.target as HTMLTextAreaElement;
                store.newCommentText = el.value;
                const q = activeMentionQuery(el.value, el.selectionStart);
                if (q !== null) {
                  store.mentionTarget = "new";
                  store.mentionQuery = q;
                  store.mentionIndex = 0;
                } else if (store.mentionTarget === "new") {
                  store.mentionTarget = null;
                }
              }}
              onKeyDown$={(e) => {
                const el = e.target as HTMLTextAreaElement;
                if (store.mentionTarget === "new") {
                  const candidates = filterMentionables(
                    mentionables,
                    store.mentionQuery,
                  );
                  if (e.key === "Escape") {
                    store.mentionTarget = null;
                    return;
                  }
                  if (candidates.length > 0) {
                    if (e.key === "ArrowDown" || e.key === "ArrowUp") {
                      e.preventDefault();
                      const step = e.key === "ArrowDown" ? 1 : -1;
                      store.mentionIndex =
                        (store.mentionIndex + step + candidates.length) %
                        candidates.length;
                      return;
                    }
                    // Plain Enter picks the highlighted name; Mod+Enter still
                    // files the note, so the submit shortcut keeps working.
                    if (
                      (e.key === "Enter" && !e.metaKey && !e.ctrlKey) ||
                      e.key === "Tab"
                    ) {
                      e.preventDefault();
                      const item = candidates[store.mentionIndex];
                      if (item) {
                        const applied = applyMention(
                          store.newCommentText,
                          item.name,
                          el.selectionStart,
                        );
                        store.newCommentText = applied.text;
                        store.mentionTarget = null;
                        restoreMentionCaret("new", applied.caret);
                      }
                      return;
                    }
                  }
                }
                if (e.key === "Enter" && (e.metaKey || e.ctrlKey)) {
                  addComment();
                }
              }}
              onBlur$={(e) => {
                if (store.mentionTarget === "new" && blurLeavesMentionUi(e)) {
                  store.mentionTarget = null;
                }
              }}
              placeholder={getCommentPlaceholder(brief)}
              class="w-full px-3 py-2 text-sm bg-[var(--color-paper-soft)] border border-[var(--color-paper-3)] resize-none focus:outline-none focus:border-[var(--color-mustard)] text-[var(--color-ink)] placeholder:text-[var(--color-ink-muted)] placeholder:italic"
              style="font-family: var(--font-serif); border-radius: 2px;"
              rows={2}
            />
            {store.mentionTarget === "new" && (
              <MentionDropdown
                id={mentionListId("new")}
                items={mentionables}
                query={store.mentionQuery}
                activeIndex={store.mentionIndex}
                size="md"
                onSelect$={$((item: Mentionable) => {
                  const el = document.getElementById(
                    mentionInputId("new"),
                  ) as HTMLTextAreaElement | null;
                  const applied = applyMention(
                    store.newCommentText,
                    item.name,
                    el?.selectionStart ?? store.newCommentText.length,
                  );
                  store.newCommentText = applied.text;
                  store.mentionTarget = null;
                  restoreMentionCaret("new", applied.caret);
                })}
              />
            )}

+ * overflows the sheet. The cap sits just above 4.2em of the default 18px
+ * body, so the house look is unchanged until the writer goes large. */

content.text:
Everything verified: **tsc clean, 108 unit tests passing, 20 e2e passing.**

## Shipped

**Marginalia @-mentions** — the mouse-pick was a Qwik QRL race: `onMouseDown$` loads asynchronously, so `preventDefault()` arrived after the blur had already unmounted the dropdown and no `click` ever fired. Replaced with declarative `preventdefault:mousedown`, added a `relatedTarget` blur guard, built the keyboard path that never existed (arrows/Enter/Tab), and made the query caret-aware so mentions work mid-sentence. `@` inside an email no longer triggers it.

**Tables** — the first row wasn't undeletable; the cell-format panel was rendered at `top + 120`, landing exactly on row 1 and eating the clicks. Finished your in-progress stack positioning, replaced the hardcoded 112/68 height guesses with measured `getBoundingClientRect`, and closed a hole where the viewport clamp could still shove an "above" stack onto the table. `deleteTable` worked all along — it was the 12th button in an 1100px row inside a 760px scroll container and wasn't in the command registry at all; now registered (slash menu + shortcuts) and pinned `sticky right-0`.

**Theming** — `[data-theme]` layer with four presets, custom overrides of the 8 core tokens, WCAG contrast warning, inline flash guard in `<head>`, synced to a new Convex `appearance` table. The bulk of the work was the 103 `rgba()` literals baked into the paper textures; I also split `--shade` from `--color-ink` so shadows darken instead of glowing on a dark ground, defined 13 tokens that were referenced but never existed, and deleted ~400 lines of dead landing-variant CSS.

**Fonts** — pagination and the toolbar were both fine. The defect was the drop cap: `::first-letter` outranks the inline styles the type controls write, so a manuscript set in Special Elite kept a Fraunces drop cap, and `4.2em` of 36pt rendered at 201px. Now inherits the family, bounded at 5rem.

**Import** — `onImported$` was never passed at the only call site. The file parsed, wrote to IndexedDB, the dialog closed, and the editor never reloaded — then autosave wrote the old manuscript back over it. Wired up, with an e2e test that proves the import survives autosave and reload.

**Scroll by default** — done, but note the design call: `pagination` drove *both* the editor view and the print page size, so a naive flip would have made every PDF `size: auto`. I left the field unset in `DEFAULT_LAYOUT` so unset resolves to continuous on screen and paginated on export; an explicit choice is honoured by both.

**One thing you need to run:** `npx convex dev` to push the new `appearance` table before theme sync works.

## Still open

- **Page overflow** (#10) — the only remaining bug. `no block straddles a sheet boundary` passes, so it's something specific your document has that the fixtures don't.
- **Toolbar on small screens** (#7)
- **Layout modal** (#8)

I'll take the overflow bug next unless you'd rather I didn't — but for the layout modal, "better" isn't something I can act on well:

content.text:
All green: **tsc clean, 113 unit tests, 20 e2e passing.**

## The page-gap bug

Your instinct about headings was right, and the mechanism is specific. In `paginate()`, the backwards `keepWithNext` walk that protects headings is bounded by `breakAt > runStart + 1`. When a heading is immediately followed by a paragraph taller than one page, that guard is *already* false — so the walk can't move, and the run closes with **nothing on the sheet but the heading**. Repeat per long paragraph, and you get the trail of near-empty pages.

The deeper cause is that blocks are atomic: a paragraph taller than the content box bleeds across sheets *wherever* it starts, so pushing it to a fresh page bought no fidelity and cost the tail of the page before it. Now an unfittable block starts where it falls and bleeds from there; only the block after it takes a break. Guarded on the run so far actually fitting, so the degenerate case (margins dragged until they meet) still falls back to one block per sheet instead of one unbounded run.

Two regression tests cover it, including `a heading is never marooned on a blank page by the paragraph it opens`.

**On your two suggestions:** horizontal margins already exist and are applied (`--doc-pad-left/right`) — they're just tight, 2rem ≈ 0.33in against a typical 1in. And I did *not* remove the heading break rule: it's what stops a heading being stranded at the bottom of a page, and it mirrors `break-after: avoid` in the print stylesheet. The stranding was the guard misfiring, not the guard being wrong.

**What I can't fix within this engine:** text genuinely drifting mid-paragraph across a boundary. Splitting a paragraph would mean fragmenting a block with decorations, which is the documented ceiling of a ProseMirror decoration engine — `pagination-geometry.ts:230` spells out why. Every browser-based word processor has the same limit. The gaps are gone; a single >1-page paragraph will still flow across the seam.

## Still open

- **#7 Toolbar on small screens**
- **#8 Layout modal** — you said "too cramped / bad layout", so I'll take it as a spacing and grouping pass, no behaviour change. Worth folding the margin defaults into that same pass, since 0.33in page margins are arguably the real reason pages look wrong — but changing them re-flows every existing document, so I'd want your call before touching it.

**Still needs you:** `npx convex dev` to push the new `appearance` table before theme sync works.
